title: The Solar System
seo_title: Year 6 Science: The Solar System Worksheets (Australian Curriculum)
standard_text: Describe the movement of Earth and other planets relative to the Sun and model how Earth's tilt, rotation on its axis and revolution around the Sun cause cycles of day and night and seasons (summary of the Australian Curriculum v9.0 Science content description).
meta_desc: Free Year 6 science worksheets on the solar system: the Sun, the eight planets in order, rocky planets and gas giants, orbits, distances and scale models. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: Rocky planets are close to the Sun; the gas and ice giants are far away.
body_html:
How to think about it

The solar system is the Sun and everything that orbits it.

  • The eight planets in order: Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune.
  • The four inner planets are small and rocky; the four outer planets are giants made mostly of gas and ice.
  • The further a planet is from the Sun, the longer it takes to orbit, and the gaps between planets get much bigger.
Example

Which planet is fourth from the Sun?

Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars

Answer: Mars

Example

Earth is 10 cm from the Sun in a model. Jupiter is 5.2 times as far. Where does it go?

5.2 × 10 cm

Answer: 52 cm

Common mistakes

  • Thinking the Sun orbits the Earth.
  • Calling the Moon a planet.
  • Spacing the planets evenly in a model.

faq.q: What are the eight planets in order?
faq.a: Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus and Neptune. A memory sentence: My Very Excellent Mother Just Served Us Noodles.

faq.q: Why is Pluto not a planet?
faq.a: Pluto is a dwarf planet. It is very small and shares its orbit with many other icy objects.

faq.q: Why do planets shine if they are not stars?
faq.a: Planets reflect light from the Sun. Only stars, like the Sun, make their own light.

items.q: For thousands of years, First Nations Australians have used the stars to know when to hunt and gather foods. What does this show?
c: Stars cannot be used for anything.
Stars change every night at random.
Observing patterns in the sky is a kind of science.
Only telescopes can study the sky.
items.e: Long-term observation of patterns is science.

items.q: Why do scientists use models of the solar system?
c: It is too big to see all at once, so models help explain it.
Models are more accurate than real data.
items.e: Models can show size or distance, but rarely both.
